keyQuestions.text: Q1: Zero-hit fallback (sweet-search core/search/grep-unindexed-fallback.js): when the committed trigger index misses because a packet is new or edited since the last index build, should the lookup re-check only git's modified and untracked spec docs? Does Skilled's lookup already do anything like this, how often is the index stale in practice, and what is the cost?

Q2: Per-file caps with an elision line (core/search/grep-output-shaping.js, grep-allocation-rules.js): does one large file (a research.md, an iteration log, a changelog) flood Skilled's ranked results today, and would a per-file cap, a one-line-per-file guarantee and a "N more hits in M files not shown" line help? Show real queries.

Q3: Meaningful-line preference (core/search/grep-line-classes.js): beyond the existing evidence-field order (trigger_phrases, title/description, anchor, body), would demoting template boilerplate (FILL comments, stock template sentences repeated in every packet) improve results? Show real queries where boilerplate matches crowd out real content.

Q4: Out-of-scope hint (core/search/grep-outside-probe.js): when a track- or packet-scoped search returns little, would a one-line "also N hits in other tracks: X, Y" help, and what does it cost on this repo?

Q5: Dedup plus final-k (core/search/span-dedupe.js, final-k.js): do runtime mirror folders (.claude/, .opencode/, .codex/ and others) or z_archive copies return the same text more than once today, given the coverage and exclusion policy in retrieval-conventions.md section 9? Would dedup and a strict final-k cut help?

keyFindings.text: **`--check` is not a substitute.** It already reports exactly this staleness, but it "costs one full corpus walk, so it runs as the report-only `advisory-checks.yml` step and by hand, never per lookup". The fallback is a zero-hit-only partial approximation of `--check`, and should be described that way rather than as a replacement. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/README.md:84]

keyFindings.text: **`git ls-files --modified --others` is the wrong candidate source; it misses staged additions.** On this checkout it returned 42 paths (15 `.md`) while `git status --porcelain -- specs` returned 109 entries (29 `.md`). The difference is staged-but-uncommitted `A ` entries, which are neither worktree-modified nor untracked. A packet created and `git add`ed before the next index build is exactly the case Q1 exists to cover, and `ls-files -m -o` would silently omit it. [INFERENCE: based on `git status --porcelain -- specs` returning 109 entries / 29 md and `git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard -- specs` returning 42 / 15 in this iteration]

keyFindings.text: **A definition of staleness already exists in Skilled, and the lookup is the one consumer that does not use it.** `lib/freshness.mjs` states the single definition: a document is stale when the phrases it declares differ from the phrases the index attributes to its path. Its two consumers are `generate-trigger-index.mjs --check` over the whole corpus and the canonical save path's `checkTriggerIndexFreshness` over one packet. Neither feeds the lookup, so the lookup can return a stale answer with no signal. keyFindings.text: **A git-aware fallback creates a contract tension the convention would have to resolve.** Section 5 promises that "two runs over an unchanged corpus therefore produce the same ordering". A fallback that adds results from the worktree makes the answer depend on uncommitted state, so two runs on the same corpus can differ. That is arguably still deterministic for a fixed worktree, but the document's claim and the lookup's exit-code contract both need an explicit amendment plus a marker field, not a silent behavior change. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md:204-212]

keyFindings.text: **Corpus-wide staleness is tiny; new-packet staleness is total.** The committed index was built at `Nov 9 11:58:23 2026`. At measurement time 39 of 67,595 spec `.md` files were newer than it (0.06%), and `git status --porcelain -- specs` listed 109 changed or untracked entries, 29 of them `.md`. Staleness is therefore rare by file count but concentrated exactly on the newest packets, which are the most likely subject of a fresh session's first prompt. [INFERENCE: based on the measured newer-file count, the changed-file count, and finding 3's absent packet]

keyFindings.text: **Skilled's keyed lookup performs no staleness check of any kind.** `loadIndex` reads and parses one artifact and returns its `indexHash` and `manifestHash`; `lookup` scores candidate phrases and sorts; the process exits `1` when no result scores above zero. There is no git call, no mtime comparison, no freshness import, and no field in the JSON answer that distinguishes "the corpus does not contain this phrase" from "the index predates this document". keyFindings.text: **The fallback is cheap when scoped and expensive when repo-wide.** Measured on this checkout: cold lookup `0.07s` without the index hash (`0.12s` with it); `git status --porcelain -- specs` `0.88-0.90s`; `git ls-files --modified --others --exclude-standard -- specs` `0.90s`; the same git call scoped to one packet `0.02-0.03s`; `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` `0.01s`; reading the frontmatter of all 15 changed `.md` files and matching the block `0.02s`. A repo-wide fallback costs roughly thirteen times the lookup it is rescuing; a packet-scoped one is close to free. [INFERENCE: based on `/usr/bin/time -p` measurements taken in this iteration against this checkout]

keyFindings.text: **The index carries no build timestamp, so sweet-search's freshness rule cannot be ported as written.** Its `indexFreshness` compares a source file's `mtimeMs` against the reconcile manifest's `publishedAt`, and returns `known: false` when that timestamp is absent. Skilled's index top-level keys are exactly `manifestHash`, `normalization`, `paths`, `phrases`, `schemaVersion` - no publish time. The file's own mtime is also untrustworthy here: the same sweet-search file records that a worktree clone gives every file the checkout's mtime, which is why it keeps a separate pending-reindex queue rather than trusting mtimes alone. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/retrieval-integrations/001-sweet-search-integration/context/sweet-search-main/core/search/index-freshness.js:17-23] [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/retrieval-integrations/001-sweet-search-integration/context/sweet-search-main/core/search/index-freshness.js:37-42] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/data/trigger-index.json]

keyFindings.text: **The lesson's scan target does not transfer unchanged.** Sweet-search's fallback greps file *contents*, because its sparse-gram index answers content questions. Skilled's keyed lane answers a different question: which document *declared* this phrase in `trigger_phrases`. The convention is explicit that the two lanes "answer different questions" and that an exact identifier goes to ripgrep first. A body-text grep over changed files would therefore return prose mentions, which belong to the free-text lane, not candidates for a keyed hit. To answer Gate 1's question for a changed document the fallback must read that document's frontmatter phrases and score them with the existing `scorePhrase`/`normalizeTriggerText` pair. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md:40-49] [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/retrieval-integrations/001-sweet-search-integration/context/sweet-search-main/core/search/grep-unindexed-fallback.js:60-79]

Adding the two topic queries from finding 3, that is 2 of 7 zero-hits. This is a probe, not a rate: the sample is too small and too self-selected to support a percentage. keyFindings.text: **sweet-search solves it with three coupled parts, not one cap.** (a) A streaming per-file cap that still counts what it drops: `applyGrepFileDiversity` keeps at most `perFileCap` per file and at most `maxFiles` files, returning `hiddenFileCount`, `hiddenMatchCount` and a `hiddenSample`. keyFindings.text: **The mechanism behind finding 2 is the rank tuple, not the file size.** `rankMatches` sorts by evidence field, then match class, then path, then line. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/rg-lane.mjs:408-411] Match class is a per-line property, so a multi-token prose query scatters classes across files and keeps the top-k diverse; a single-token query makes nearly every line the same class (`phrase-containment`), after which the path tie-break groups one file's lines contiguously and a k cut takes that file's block first. [INFERENCE: derived from the four measured query shapes and the sort key order at rg-lane.mjs:408-411]

keyFindings.text: **Real keyed query: template copies take three of six slots and outrank a real packet.** Query `acceptance criteria closure gate` returned two real packets at `exact` 1.0, then the level-2, level-3 and level-3+ acceptance-criteria template copies at `query-containment` 0.88, then a real packet at `token-overlap` 0.75. The three template copies are indexed by their own placeholder phrases (`acceptance criteria`, `closure gate`, `ac traceability`, `waiver adr`). [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/examples/level-2/acceptance-criteria.md:5] The judge names those same phrases `template-default` and only warns — a warning never deletes an author's phrase. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/phrase-judge.mjs:121] Because the class is not persisted in the index, the lookup cannot distinguish a template copy from an authored declaration, and path order decides inside the tie.

keyFindings.text: **The match-class component is degenerate for fixed-string matches.** `rankMatches` scores the matched *line text* against the query, and a fixed-string hit always contains the query, so every hit lands in the same containment class. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/rg-lane.mjs:396] The sort then falls through to evidence field, path and line. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/rg-lane.mjs:408] Observed directly: 784 `body` rows ordered by path. Inside `body` the tuple carries no content signal, which is exactly the gap a line class would fill.

keyFindings.text: **The sweet-search mechanism does not transfer; its principle does.** Its classes come from code-graph entities — class 0 declaration, class 1 inside a symbol span, class 2 outside — and are gated on the file being no newer than the published index. keyFindings.text: **Skilled's keyed lane already computes the out-of-scope answer and throws it away.** In `lookup()`, the posting loop resolves `documentPath` and the scored match class/score *before* the scope test, and the scope test is a bare `continue`. Counting the rejected documents, and tallying their top-level path segment, is one `Map` increment at that exact point — no second read, no subprocess, no index beyond the one already parsed. keyFindings.text: **sweet-search's probe is conditional on a persistent index, so its mechanism cannot transfer.** `probeOutsideScope` returns `null` — meaning "run the exact search instead" — unless a sparse gram index exists and answers `queryLiterals`, and it declines again when the candidate pool is at or under the exact threshold. Past that threshold it reads at most 512 candidate files (2048 when the scope itself answered nothing) and reports `N+ files` when the pool was capped. Every constant in that file exists to bound a whole-repo grep: the header states the cost model directly, "~11 us a file on kubernetes … 33 ms for 3,023 … 300-800 ms for a license header in 26,000". ruledOutDirections.text: **`git ls-files --modified --others` as the candidate source.** Rejected on measured coverage: it loses 14 of 29 changed `.md` files, all staged additions.
**Body-text grep over changed files as the fallback mechanism.** Rejected on contract: the keyed lane matches declared phrases, not prose.
**Porting `indexFreshness` verbatim.** Rejected on evidence: Skilled's index has no `publishedAt`, and checkout mtimes are not a build-time proxy.
**Running `--check` on zero-hit.** Rejected on documented cost: a full corpus walk, explicitly never per lookup.

**Adopting `perFileCap` alone.** One line per file still returns 13,113 rows corpus-wide for a single common token, so it does not bound output on its own. [INFERENCE: corpus-wide file count measured with the count recipe]

**Copying sweet-search's weighted allocation (Sainte-Laguë / `sat2`) into Skilled.** Would create a second relevance ranker beside the evidence-field/match-class tuple; the tuple already breaks the tie the allocation would be guessing at. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md:202-212]

**Measuring the flood with a shell sort.** A `sort -t: -k1,1 -k2,2n | head -20` emulation of the rank tuple reported 20 of 20 top lines from a single file for `deep research`, which the real ranker contradicts (15 distinct files in the same top 20). The emulation dropped the match-class component that precedes the path tie-break, so it manufactured a flood that the shipped ranker does not produce for that query. Re-measured by calling `search('structured', …)` directly; only the real-ranker numbers are used above. Candidate for "exhausted approaches": do not emulate the rank tuple with `sort`.

**Per-file cap on the trigger-index lane.** Structurally impossible to need: one row per document already. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:226-239]
**Applying line classes to the keyed lane.** It returns documents, not lines (Finding 1). No code change there can express the lesson.

**Demoting `template-default` phrases by deleting them.** The convention explicitly refuses to delete an author's phrase, so any fix must demote at rank time, not remove at generation time. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/phrase-judge.mjs:91]

**Porting `classifyGrepLines` / `selectGrepLinesByClass` as written.** Both need a symbol entity list and an index-freshness predicate (Finding 6); adopting them would require the persistent index the topic forbids.

**Treating `FILL` as the boilerplate to demote.** It survives once per template example file and not across authored packets, so demoting it would buy almost nothing (Finding 4). The stock prose sentences are the real pollutant.

**A literal port of `probeOutsideScope`.** It requires `ensureSparseGramIndex` and a queryable gram index; the hard constraint forbids a persistent index and `retrieval-conventions.md` names vector/BM25/stateful retrieval as a declared loss. A port would return `null` on every call here.
**Firing the hint on every scoped ripgrep query.** 0.77 s against 0.012 s is a 64x tax on the common path to help the rare one.
**Firing the hint on the keyed lane's unscoped zero.** With no scope supplied there is nothing out of scope, and the observed zero was a phrase miss (0 unscoped) rather than a scope miss.
**Treating `truncated` as the existing hint.** It reports the result cap, not the scope boundary; the scoped run above had `truncated: false` and still hid 3 documents in other tracks.
